description: Flood banks and river walls the OS five-foot plan (1893-96) draws in the core box whose crests the model drew well below the OS wall-top and bank-top readings on them (task E, 5 October 2026; author: 'fix the rivers'). Each bank is traced along the middle of its hatched band (or the wall line) in the scene frame; its crest runs through the OS readings on it, interpolated by chainage and held beyond the end readings. scripts/build_main_landscape.py raises the land to this profile (never lowers it, never inside drawn water): the crest over crestHalfWidthMetres either side of the line, then side slopes of sideSlope horizontal to 1 vertical down to the ground.
frame: scene x = easting - 538900, z = 183209 - northing; levels are scene y metres (docs/data/ground-plan.json origin)
source: OS London five-foot plan, 1893-96 (reference/nls-tiles/os-london-five-foot-1893, read through scripts/factory_map_sources.py mosaic at zoom 18); readings from data/maps/os-ground-levels.json

banks.name: Long Wall (Mill Meads flood bank, west side of the Channelsea and Abbey Creek)
banks.evidence: Mapped: the hatched embankment lettered LONG WALL, with F.P. along its top, from the Channelsea river wall at the mouth (-400, 465) to the bend beside Abbey Creek and north to the embankment west of the Channelsea (-48, 78); the saltings between it and the creek lie below the H.W.M.O.T. Observed: 17.1-18.1 ft on its top (2.98-3.29 m). Before this record the model drew no bank on this line: its only bank was a 2 m strip at the tidal outline 20-30 m east, and the hatched bank itself was low marsh. Estimated: the crest width (the footpath) and the side slope (the hatching is about 9 m wide).

banks.name: Channelsea east bank from the Northern Outfall Sewer to the West Ham Chemical Works river wall and the Oil and Stearine Works
banks.evidence: Mapped: the hatched bank with F.P. on its top curving from the Northern Outfall Sewer embankment (50, 39) round to the works (1, 153), 20-30 m east of the water, the model's tidal outline covering the foreshore in front of it; the river wall (double line) along the works frontage from z 190 to 273 and the hatched bank north of it and south-west of the drain outfall towards the Oil and Stearine Works. Observed: 17.1-17.9 ft (2.98-3.22 m). The model drew the crest at 2.0-2.5 m with a notch of 0.72 m at z 153, through which the whole marsh east of the Channelsea filled at 2.56 m ODN (task E flood grid). Estimated: the made ground behind the wall (crest width and slope). No reading on the curved bank north of the works: its crest holds the first reading (17.4 ft), an estimate. The line starts on the outfall sewer's south slope (47.5, 27) so that it closes against the embankment; the sewer's crossing of the Channelsea is drawn as a deck and its toe left a trough.

banks.name: Short Wall (east bank of the Three Mills Wall River) and the river-wall path north of it
banks.evidence: Mapped: the hatched bank lettered SHORT WALL along the east side of the Three Mills Wall River, and north of it the hatched strip carrying the river-wall path between the Wall River and the channel to the east, up to the High Street. Observed: 16.7-17.9 ft (2.86-3.22 m). The model drew 1.65-2.78 m. Estimated: crest width and side slope.

notTraced: The bank west of Mill Meads along x -405 (hatched, no reading on it), the Wall River west bank by the Asphalte Works (hatched, no reading) and the Harrow Bridge Wharf bank (drawn 0.27 m under its readings) are left as drawn.
